name: Japan

facts.religion: Shinto and Buddhist practice widely shared, few formally religious

snapshot: Sanae Takaichi, Japan's first woman prime minister, won a two-thirds supermajority in a February 2026 snap election, the LDP's biggest win ever, on a hard line toward Beijing.
culture: Japan blends deep tradition, from tea ceremony and Shinto shrines to the imperial line, the world's oldest monarchy, with global pop culture: anime, manga, video games and J-pop. Seasonal rituals like cherry blossom viewing are national events. Baseball and sumo are the top sports, and Shohei Ohtani is a national hero.
society: Japan has the world's oldest population; nearly 30 percent are over 65, and the population is shrinking. A weak yen has fuelled record tourism. Long working hours, low birth rates and a gender gap in pay and leadership are persistent issues. Immigration is rising slowly, a politically sensitive change.
situation: Japan went through five prime ministers in five years, each weaker than the last, while the long-ruling Liberal Democratic Party lost its majority in 2024 amid a slush-fund scandal. Then in October 2025 the party chose Sanae Takaichi, a hard-line conservative who admires Margaret Thatcher, as Japan's first woman prime minister. Within weeks she said Japan could respond militarily if China attacked Taiwan, the most direct statement by any sitting Japanese leader. China was furious and hit back where it hurt: it told its citizens not to travel to Japan, restricted seafood imports and even took back Japan's last two pandas (AFP via Edition.mv).

Takaichi bet that voters would side with her. She called a snap election in the middle of winter, only the third February vote since the war, and on 8 February the LDP won 315 of 465 seats, a two-thirds supermajority on its own for the first time in its 70-year history (Stanford APARC). The victory gives her the numbers to push higher military spending, a $135 billion stimulus and tax cuts that have rattled bond markets worried about Japan's enormous debt, and possibly to revise the pacifist constitution. Analysts read the result as voters endorsing her stand against Beijing's pressure. Japan has gone from a revolving door to one of the strongest governments among the rich democracies, led by a nationalist.
power: A constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system. The emperor is symbolic; the prime minister is chosen by the Diet, mainly the 465-seat House of Representatives, and leads the cabinet. The upper House of Councillors can delay legislation, and a two-thirds vote in both houses plus a referendum is needed to amend the constitution.
holders: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi (LDP), in office since October 2025.
